name: Cable One Arm Curl
description: A biceps curl that lifts the load from a full stretch to a hard squeeze with the palms up, keeping the elbows pinned to the sides so the biceps do the work. Performed with a cable.
instructions: Stand tall holding the handle with your palms facing up and your arms hanging straight down.
Pin your elbows to your sides and brace your core — your upper arms stay still the whole set.

name: Dumbbell Incline Biceps Curl
description: An incline curl performed with the arms hanging behind the torso to bias the long (outer) head of the biceps. Performed with a dumbbell.
instructions: Sit back on an incline bench so your arms hang straight down behind your torso, holding the weight with your palms up.
Let your shoulders relax back and keep your upper arms still — this stretch is what biases the long head.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders without letting your elbows drift forward.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top for a count.
Lower the weight slowly back to the full stretch, keeping the tension on your biceps the whole way.

name: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl
description: A hammer curl with a neutral, thumbs-up grip that drives the brachialis and brachioradialis along with the biceps. Performed with a dumbbell.
instructions: Stand tall holding the weight with a neutral, thumbs-up grip and your arms hanging straight.
Pin your elbows to your sides and keep your wrists straight in that neutral position.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders, keeping your thumbs pointing up the whole way.
Squeeze your biceps and forearms at the top for a count.
Lower the weight slowly back down under control, keeping your upper arms still.

name: EZ Barbell Reverse Grip Curl
description: A reverse curl with an overhand, palms-down grip that shifts the work onto the brachioradialis and wrist extensors. Performed with an ez / sz bar.
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar with an overhand, palms-down grip and your arms hanging straight.
Pin your elbows to your sides and keep your wrists firm and straight.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders, leading with the backs of your hands so the work lands on your forearms.
Squeeze the brachioradialis and biceps at the top.
Lower the bar slowly back down under control, keeping your elbows pinned and your wrists locked.

name: Dumbbell Single Arm Preacher Curl
description: A preacher curl with the upper arms fixed on the pad, curling from a deep stretch to kill momentum and load the short (inner) head. Performed with a dumbbell.
instructions: Set your upper arms flat on the preacher pad and hold the weight with your palms up and arms extended.
Keep your arms fixed on the pad — the angle kills momentum and loads the short head.
Curl the weight up from the deep stretch toward your shoulders, squeezing your biceps.
Hold the contraction briefly at the top.
Lower the weight slowly until your arms are almost straight, staying in control. Never bounce out of the bottom stretch.

name: Lever Preacher Curl

description: An overhead extension that biases the long head of the triceps through a deep stretch behind the head. Performed with a cable.
instructions: Set up tall with the rope raised overhead and your arms fully extended, elbows pointing forward.
Keep your elbows high and close to your head — this is the key to working the long head.
Bend at the elbows and lower the rope behind your head until you feel a deep stretch in your triceps.
Drive the rope back up to full lockout by straightening your arms, keeping your upper arms still.
Keep your ribs down and core braced so your lower back doesn't arch.

Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with your arms straight.
Lower the bar toward your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked in close to your body.
